root_cause: Hourly job 116 runs contact context and fourteen expensive commercial tasks within one PG cron statement; repeated SQL timeout aborts the entire combined execution. Query profiling shows portfolio view count can be computed in roughly three seconds, so simply raising a global timeout is unjustified.
action: Reuse existing job 116 and fourteen functions, execute one stage per transaction at distinct minutes 3 through 42 each hour; leave contact assessment to job 138. Track typed internal stage receipts; never substitute those for provider delivery receipts.
observation: Several cron #116 statements timed out after 120 seconds on 2026-10-11, starving later independent sales and learning stages.
root_cause_hypothesis: The single job invokes source refresh plus fourteen stages within one statement budget; isolating stages reuses existing cron and prevents failure cascading.
prevention: Existing cron #116 executes one canonical commercial function per separate scheduled transaction, with independently observed job success/failure; no additional queue, sender, CRM or permission bypass.
limitations: Release candidate only: stage heartbeat and independent provider delivery must be verified after protected merge; a static test is not production proof.
